name: Residential Mortgage Application — Down-Valuation Exception Path
description: Exception path EX-001: the surveyor's valuation amount is less than the purchase price. The bank's maximum loan is recalculated against the lower valuation amount. The customer is notified and offered three options: renegotiate purchase price, increase deposit to maintain LTV, or withdraw application. This diagram picks up from the start of PH-012 (Valuation) and shows the exception resolution.
preconditions: Full application submitted and hard credit check completed (PH-011 complete)
Valuation type: drive-by survey (LTV >= 75% threshold triggered full surveyor instruction)

steps.label: Determine valuation type: LTV = 75% → drive-by survey (not desktop AVM). Create ENT-014 PropertyValuation (status: instructed, type: drive_by). Transition application status: valuation_pending.
Publish EVT-024 ValuationInstructed (application_id, valuation_id, type: drive_by)
Instruct drive-by survey via surveyor panel. SLA: 2–3 business days.
2 business days elapse. Surveyor conducts drive-by inspection.
Valuation report received: valuation_amount = £355,000 (vs purchase price £390,000). DOWN-VALUATION.

Update ENT-014 PropertyValuation:
- valuation_amount: 355000
- valuation_date: today
- status: completed
- down_valuation_flag: TRUE (355000 < 390000)
Recalculate LTV on ENT-012:
- New LTV = 292500 / 355000 = 82.39%
- Original LTV was 75.00% — now exceeds product limit (max 80% for this product)
Transition application status: valuation_complete.
Publish EVT-025 ValuationCompleted (application_id, valuation_amount: 355000, down_valuation_flag: TRUE, recalculated_ltv: 82.39)
Consume EVT-025 (down_valuation_flag: true). Trigger down-valuation customer notification.

Email: Down-valuation notification.
Surveyor valued property at £355,000 vs. purchase price £390,000.
Your options:
1. Renegotiate purchase price down to £355,000
2. Increase deposit by £35,000 (new deposit: £132,500) to keep LTV at 75%
3. Withdraw application
Please respond within 28 days.
Customer reviews options with solicitor / financial adviser. Customer decides to increase deposit.
Select option 2: Increase deposit by £35,000. New deposit: £132,500. New loan: £257,500.

Update ENT-012 MortgageApplication:
- deposit_amount: 132500
- loan_amount: 257500
- ltv_ratio: 257500/355000 = 72.54% ✓ (within 80% product limit)
Affordability reassessment triggered: new monthly payment recalculated.
200 OK. Application updated. New LTV: 72.54%. Proceeding to underwriting.
Notification: Application updated with new deposit amount. Proceeding to underwriting.

Application enters underwriting queue. PER-055 assigned.
Transition status: underwriting.
PER-055 notified of down-valuation history and amended deposit.

PER-055 reviews amended application:
- New loan: £257,500 @ LTV 72.54% ✓
- Affordability with reduced loan: re-run stress test — PASS ✓
- Credit score: 715 PASS ✓
- Down-valuation noted and resolved (deposit increased)
Decision: APPROVE (reduced loan amount)
Journey continues on happy path from PH-014 (Mortgage Offer) with amended loan amount of £257,500.

alternative_resolution_paths.description: If customer renegotiates purchase price down to £355,000: original deposit (£97,500) now represents 27.5%. New LTV: 267,500/355,000 = 75.35% — still within product limit but requires new property purchase price on application. Stamp duty recalculation may apply.
alternative_resolution_paths.steps_affected: Steps 12–15 replaced: customer updates purchase_price to 355000. New loan_amount: 257500. LTV: 72.54%.

alternative_resolution_paths.description: Customer withdraws application. ENT-012 status transitions to 'withdrawn'. No refund of valuation fee. FOS signpost provided if customer disputes bank's process.
alternative_resolution_paths.steps_affected: From step 10: customer selects withdraw. SVC-002 transitions status to 'withdrawn'. EVT-022 tombstone published. No further processing.
